decision_titles: Historical signage for Nipper Maher Park
plain_text:
The Waltham Parks-Recreation Board held the October Board meeting on Wednesday, October 
14, 2026, at the Waltham Recreation Department, 510 Moody St, Waltham, MA 02453.  
Present were Debra Coleman, John Graceffa, Jennie Scafidi, Stacey Tully, Gary Vallerand, and 
Jerry Walker. Absent were Tom Creonte and Patricia Curtin. 
Also present were Director Kim Hebert and Assistant Director Ed Kelley II. 
Chairperson Jerry Walker called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.  
A moment of silence was held in memory of Mr. William Creonte, Sr. 
Cyd Abnet, Waltham Times, was recognized as recording the meeting. 
A motion was then made to approve the minutes of September 9, 2026, Parks-Recreation Board 
meeting by Gary Vallerand and seconded by Debra Coleman. All other Board Members were in 
favor.  
The monthly bills for FY 27 were circulated and signed by all Parks-Recreation Board Members.  
Director Hebert reviewed the statement of accounts and explained that the accounts detailed the 
current balances in operational and capital budget accounts. The accounts on the statements had 
all been updated. Many capital accounts have been closed out as the projects were completed at 
the end of the last fiscal year. All accounts are in good standing.  
A motion to move agenda item out of order was made by Gary Vallerand and seconded by Debra 
Coleman. All were in favor. 
Lawrence School Building- Mayor McCarthy was next on the agenda. Director Hebert presented 
a communication requesting guidance for the future of the former Lawrence School and 
property. The decision needing guidance would be to renovate the existing building or demolish 
it for a new recreation amenity. There has been discussion about building an ice hockey rink 
somewhere within the 200 Trapelo Road property. The Mayor respectfully requested the Parks-
Recreation Board’s to vote to appoint Director Hebert to an exploratory committee of City 
Council members for a potential hockey rink. 
A motion to approve Director Hebert to an exploratory committee with City Council members on 
a potential plan for a hockey rink was made by John Graceffa and seconded by Debra Coleman. 
Next on the agenda was Waltham Youth Baseball, represented by Joe Lafauci and Chris Jensen. 
Mr. Lafauci and Mr. Jensen reported a successful season. The program expects to raise fees by 
$25; the first-time prices have increased in about a decade. Additionally, a summer program was 
held at Babe Ruth, as well as a free “Sandlot” program for the younger participants.  The Parks-
Recreation Board thanked Mr. Lafauci and Mr. Jensen for their efforts and dedication to the 
league.
Waltham Girls Softball was next on the agenda, represented by League President Alena Gelfusa, 
and the Waltham Girls Softball Board. The League representatives reported a successful season 
and explained how it strategically schedules games and practices around other youth sports 
schedules so that participants can play in as many programs as they’d like with minimal 
conflicts. The Board thanked the league representatives for their efforts. 
Historical Signage for Nipper Maher Park would be rescheduled to a later date. 
Next on the agenda was Request for Lights at Nipper Maher Park. In the Board’s folder was a 
letter of request from Waltham Youth Baseball. The request was to add lights to one or both little 
league fields at Nipper Maher Park so that more weekday night games can be played. Following 
Board discussion, a public input meeting will be held with abutters to the 65 Dartmouth property, 
and the item will be brought back to the Parks-Recreation Board for final approval. 
Director’s Report: 
October Facilities updates-  
• Veterans Skating Rink- Weekday public skating and adult hockey are occurring with 
weekend public skating beginning in November  
• Mini Golf at 200 Trapelo will be open on Saturdays from 12:00pm – 4:00 pm through 
October 31st. 
• Pickleball reservations for 119 School Street opened on October 1st. 
• Pavilion rentals will close at the end of October.  
• Prospect Hill Park vehicle access road will close at the end of October. 
 
Construction Projects-  
Green Acres continues to work on grading, the athletic area parking lot and site amenities.  
The demolition project is completed for all three buildings 
Northern Contracting is finishing window installation in the Administration Building and Howe.  
The final punch list items are being completed. 
The City’s Engineering Department’s utility project is ongoing at 200 Trapelo. 
Design work for the nine-hole par three course with Beals & Thomas is completed. The project 
will be going out to bid soon. Funding will be requested when the bid results are received.  
The contract for design services for the indoor swimming pool is underway. It is anticipated to 
have pool construction out to bid by the end of the calendar year.  
The Nipper Maher Playground surfacing project is underway with ADA improvements to the 
play elements.
A motion to adjourn the meeting was made by John Graceffa and seconded by Gary Vallerand. 
All were in favor.  
The meeting adjourned at 6:20 p.m. 
Respectfully Submitted, 
 
Ed Kelley 
Assistant Director of Recreation
